A unique fuzz using MOSFETs and NOS components The Mos Fuzz is a unique circuit that is an expansion of the Bazz Fuss but it uses MOSFETs to create a smoother and less gritty fuzz. It has a lot more bass than a traditional fuzz and has insane cleanup with your guitar's volume knob. The frequency response is flat and covers the full range of the guitar without excess noise that can be found in fuzz pedals. As the FUZZ knob is turned down the distorted signal can have a bit of a velcro quality that sounds like a dying battery. Depending on the strength of the guitar pickup, the fuzz control will respond differently and the sound of the pedal will vary widely.   Controls VOL: controls the volume of the pedal FUZZ: controls the amount of fuzz available, as the knob is turned down the tone will add a bit more bass and have a more muddy tone on the lower strings.  The MOS Fuzz is made with high quality components including japanese made Lumberg power and audio jacks, alpha pots and Gorva footswitch. I also used NOS components like ½ watt carbon comp resistors, Philips and Sprague capacitors, vintage silicon diodes, and NOS BS170P MOSFETs.
